chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: Now, let's talk about naming

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: conventions. So, we have different

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: conventions for naming our variables and

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: constants, and different teams prefer

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: different conventions. So, there is

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: really no right or wrong here. But, let

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: me show you the popular conventions. So,

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: earlier we declared a variable called

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: file size.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: The way we name this variable follows

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: what we call the snake case.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: So, with this convention, we have to use

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: lowercase letters to name our variables

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: and constants. And if we have multiple

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: words, we should separate them using an

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: underscore.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: Now, we have another convention called

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: Pascal case, in which we should

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: capitalize the first letter of every

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: word. So, the same variable using Pascal

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: case looks like this.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: This is Pascal case. And by the way, the

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: text that I put here, that starts with

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: two forward slashes, this is called a

chunks.text: comment. We'll talk about comments later

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: in this section, but for now, just

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: remember that comments are a way to

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: describe our code. They don't get

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: compiled, okay?

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: Now, we have another convention that is

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: similar to Pascal case. The only

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: difference is that the first letter of

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: the first word should be lowercase. So,

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: file size.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: This is camel case.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: We also have Hungarian notation, which

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: is a pretty old notation and it's not

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: relevant anymore. With Hungarian

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: notation, we should prefix the name of

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: their type. So, here we have an integer,

chunks.text: so we use a lower case I and then file

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: size, just like Pascal case. This is

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: called Hungarian notation.

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: Now, quite frankly, this is very old

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: notation. It's not relevant anymore, but

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: I still see people using it. I've seen

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: it a lot in Windows source code. The

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: reason this is not relevant anymore is

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: because in the old days we didn't have

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: good editors. So, if you declared a

chunks.title: C++ Programming Full Course (Demo)
chunks.text: variable somewhere and we wanted to know

chunks.text: its type, we had to scroll up to find

chunks.text: So, these are the popular conventions

chunks.text: out there. In this course, I'm going to
